title: The papers want {name} dropped
text: Gary Haddon has {name} on the back page after a poor few weeks and says he should make way. {first} has rated {form} over his last three games. The average {role_word} rates {role_avg}.

unanswered.why: You said nothing when the papers went after him
unanswered.text: You say nothing. {first} reads the back page on his own.

choices.label: Drop {first} this week

effects.why: You dropped him after the papers pushed

choices.result: {name} sits out this week.

choices.label: Keep {first} in

effects.why: You kept him in when the papers wanted him out

choices.result: {name} stays in the side.

title: Kev Pollard has sprayed you on radio
text: Outer Wing Radio: "{club} have lost their way and the coach has lost the players." Do you bite?

choices.label: Hit back in the presser
choices.result: You hit back. The players love it; the board winces.

choices.label: Let your footy do the talking
choices.result: You say nothing. The players hear it all week anyway.

title: {name} has been offered a newspaper column
text: A weekly piece in the Sunday paper. Good money, and a lot of opinions.

choices.label: Let {first} write it

effects.why: You let him write his column

choices.result: {name}'s first column runs on Sunday. The board will be reading every word.

choices.label: Knock it back

effects.why: You knocked back his newspaper column
Players keep their opinions out of the papers

choices.result: {name} turns the paper down.

title: Footy Tonight want a feature on {name}
text: Trish Lomax wants a week with {first}. Good for the club, and a lot of spotlight on a kid.

choices.label: Do the feature
choices.result: The feature goes to air. {first} has had a camera on him all week.

choices.label: Keep {first} out of it
choices.result: No feature. {first} would have liked it, but his week stays on his footy.

title: The Siren has your side before it's announced
text: Someone at the club is talking to Gary Haddon.

choices.label: Find the leak
choices.result: You go looking. Everyone feels watched.

choices.label: Let it go

effects.why: Nobody in the group was put under suspicion over the leak

choices.result: You let it go. The board isn't happy.

title: Footy Tonight want cameras in the rooms
text: Trish Lomax wants a behind-the-scenes piece while you're winning.

choices.label: Let the cameras in
choices.result: The cameras are in. Some of the players hate it.

choices.label: The rooms stay ours

effects.why: You kept the cameras out of the rooms

choices.result: No cameras. The board wanted the exposure.

title: {name} wants to front the group
text: You kept {name} in when the papers wanted him out. He asks for five minutes with the group at the review to answer the papers' story himself.

choices.label: Let {first} front the group

effects.why: You let him front the group

effects.held_result: {name} takes the group through it and they hear him out.
effects.failed_result: It doesn't land with the group.

choices.rule: The players listen to a teammate whose Leadership rating is {holds_at} or better. If {name} rates you {holds_opinion_at} out of 100 or better, {holds_trust_at} is enough. {name}: Leadership {leadership}, rates you {opinion} out of 100.

choices.label: Keep it between you two

effects.why: You kept it between you two when he asked for the group

choices.result: You talk it through with {name} alone. The review stays on the footy.

title: Radio says {name} is playing in the wrong spot
text: A former player on the radio says {name} should be playing as a {trial_word}. {first} wants to know if you'll try it.

choices.label: Leave {first} where he is

effects.why: You said no when he asked to try the move
You kept selection off the radio

choices.result: {name} stays in his role.

choices.label: Try {first} as a {trial_word}

effects.why: You tried him in the role he asked about

choices.result: You try {name} as a {trial_word}.

unanswered.why: You said nothing when he asked about the move
unanswered.text: You say nothing. {first} is left waiting for an answer.

title: {name} did well as a {trial_word} as a {trial_word}
text: {first} rated {trial_avg} as a {trial_word} over the three games. The average {trial_word} rates {trial_par}. {trial_tail}

choices.label: Good to hear
choices.result: {name} goes back to his usual spot, and you know he can play as a {trial_word}. Three weeks in a new role came out of the work on his own game.

title: {name}'s trial as a {trial_word} is over
text: {first} rated {trial_avg} as a {trial_word} over the three games. The average {trial_word} rates {trial_par}. {trial_tail}

choices.label: Fair enough

effects.why: You were straight with him that the move hasn't landed yet

choices.result: {name} is back in his usual spot.

title: Grand Final week
text: The Brownlow on Monday, media day, the parade on Friday. Somewhere in there, you have to train.

choices.label: Do all of it
choices.result: The players soak up every minute, and they're tired by Friday.

choices.label: The bare minimum
choices.result: In and out of the parade, no Brownlow. The sponsors grumble to the board.

title: {paper} has {club} finishing {pred_word}
text: {writer} has the club finishing {pred_word} this season, outside the finals. The papers want your answer.

unanswered.text: You say nothing. The papers have the last word.

choices.label: Say that's about right

effects.why: You were straight with the press about where the list sits

choices.result: You tell the press that's about where the list is.

choices.label: Say the ladder gets sorted on the field
choices.result: You tell the press the ladder gets sorted on the field. The board wanted something to sell memberships on.

choices.label: Say the club will finish {claim_word} or better
choices.result: You tell the press the club will finish {claim_word} or better.

title: {paper} asks how long you have
text: {writer} has the club finishing {pred_word}. The board's goal is to {goal_line}. {writer} asks if you're under pressure.

unanswered.text: You say nothing. The question stays in the papers.

choices.label: Say the board is entitled to ask
choices.result: You tell the press the board is entitled to ask, and so is the paper. The back page runs it as a coach under pressure, and the players read it.

choices.label: Say you only think about Round 1
choices.result: You tell the press you're only thinking about Round 1. The board hears a coach ducking the question.

choices.label: Say the club will finish {claim_word} or better
choices.result: You tell the press the club will finish {claim_word} or better.

title: {writer} tips {name} to break out
text: {writer} says {name} is the one to watch this year, and asks whether you agree.

unanswered.why: You said nothing when the papers tipped him
unanswered.text: You say nothing. {first} reads it on his own.

choices.label: Say {first} has earned it

effects.why: You backed him when the papers tipped him

choices.result: You tell the press {name} has earned it. A few who've done more read that too.

choices.label: Say {first} still has plenty to prove

effects.why: Nobody gets talked up before the job is done
You played down the papers' tip

choices.result: You tell the press {name} still has plenty to prove.

choices.label: Promise {first} a run in the side

effects.why: You promised him a run after the papers tipped him

choices.result: You tell the press {name} will get a run in the side.

title: You said {words_word}. {club} is {ladder_word}
text: Before the season you told the press {club} would finish {words_word} or better. It sits {ladder_word}, and the papers have thrown your words back at you.

unanswered.text: You say nothing. The papers keep your words in print.

choices.label: Say you got it wrong
choices.result: You tell the press you got it wrong. The players see you wear it, not them.

choices.label: Say the season is not over
choices.result: You tell the press the season is not over.

title: One win from the Grand Final
text: Everyone outside the club wants to talk about the last Saturday in September. You need the players thinking about this week.

choices.label: No Grand Final talk at the club

effects.why: You banned Grand Final talk in prelim week

choices.result: Anyone who says the words buys the coffees. Nobody slips. It's a tight week around the club.

choices.label: Let them dream a little
choices.result: The players talk about the big day. Training is a bit loose.

title: Most of the tips have {opp} winning
text: They finished above you, and the papers have noticed. The reporters ask if you've seen the tips.

choices.label: Pin the tips up in the rooms
choices.result: Every tip for {opp} goes on the noticeboard. The players read them twice, and some will play the game in their heads all week.

choices.label: Back your players in the press

effects.why: You backed your players in the press before a final

choices.result: "We finished below them. We've beaten better sides." The players notice. It's on the record if the final goes wrong.

title: One week short
text: A preliminary final lost. The first question in the press conference: has this list gone as far as it can?

choices.label: This group isn't done

effects.why: You told the press this group isn't done
No spot was put on notice after the prelim

choices.result: "We'll be back here, and we'll go one better."

choices.label: Nobody's spot is safe

effects.why: You told the press nobody's spot was safe after the prelim

choices.result: "We'll look hard at the list and at how we play. Nobody's spot is safe." The players read every word.
